articles.summary: If you run data governance in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), the context that matters most probably lives somewhere other than S3. Think of how an object is classified, which retention policy applies to it, where the data may reside, and whether it holds personally identifiable information (PII). You typically keep that context in a separate database, one system away from the objects it describes. Amazon S3 annotations closes that gap. You can attach the governance context directly to the S3 object, without rewriting the object. A single object version can carry up to 1,000 annotations.
